_note: whole has no patterns here on purpose. A wildcard on item code can't express 'not ground, not liquid, not meal', so FoodTagRegistry.ResolveStaticTags applies whole as the form-axis default instead: any collectible with a source tag or vanilla nutrition that matches none of ground/liquid/meal gets whole. Patterns elsewhere in this file fall into three kinds: (1) patterns that match live vanilla food; (2) patterns that match real vanilla codes carrying no nutritionProps, kept for a future admin/compat grant -- carcass-*, drycarcass-*, fishraw-*, flour-*, bone-*, bonemeal, resin*, salt, saltpeter; (3) patterns that can never match because the item computes nutrition from its live contents at runtime, not static nutritionProps -- bowl-*-meal, pie-*. Kinds (2) and (3) show up as zero-match patterns in extract.py's report -- see DEAD_PATTERN_NOTES there for the per-pattern triage; do not delete them on the strength of a zero match alone. The state axis has no fallback default: a missing state tag is a legitimate value, not a gap. About 101 vanilla foods (fungus, fresh fruit, insect, seed, most leaf/root/dairy) have no meaningful raw/cooked/preserved/spoiled distinction and are correctly left state-less. Charred codes are also deliberately unstated: a Dwarf gains little from charred food and should not be punished for it either.
